brief: Every walker in the town arrives alone; the only pair is the picnic (`a.mate`, set at spawn, judged once). From the wide shot a town where nobody walks WITH anybody reads as a queue. Send some arrivals in twos: a lane or east spawn that, at a band, spawns a companion on the SAME itinerary a step behind, held as a pair by the follower-rate law (the follower re-targets a point beside the leader several times a second, never further than one bout's travel), sharing the leader's stops (the pair sits together, browses the stall together, and a seat refusal by one takes both — `a.mate` already does this for picnic). Companions must count under the SAME cap they came from (laneCap/eastCap), not beside it, so the population is unchanged; measure the share of arrivals that are pairs at the CHOICE and the pair's separation histogram.
successLooksLike: A 10-seed daylight probe prints ~15–25 % of lane/east arrivals as pairs; the separation histogram sits between 0.9 and 1.6 cells for >90 % of samples (never under 0.9 — the merge law); laneCount/eastCount peaks unchanged vs HEAD; seats-out.mjs 0 splits; a 30-min crop of the lane shows two people side by side who arrive and leave together; naming a companion says who they are with.
avoid: Do not give pairs their own arrival source. Do not make both members pathfind independently to the same waypoint — that is the 0.9-cell failure. Do not pair kids, dogs, homers or the concert crowd this iteration.
